title: The Brake and Its Two Routes

scenes.visual: Title card: The Brake and Its Two Routes.

scenes.tts: How can nuclei that never reach the spinal cord decide whether a movement goes ahead?
scenes.visual: The deep nuclei from chapter one, with no line to the cord. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: How can nuclei that never reach the spinal cord decide whether a movement goes ahead?

scenes.tts: Start with a picture: a column of boxes. The cortex is at the top, then an input stage.
scenes.visual: Unlabelled shapes stack into a column. The top box is labelled cortex, the next input stage.
scenes.narration: Start with a picture: a column of boxes. The cortex is at the top, then an input stage.

scenes.tts: An output stage feeds the thalamus, which sends an arrow back to the cortex, closing a loop.
scenes.visual: A box near the bottom lights up, labelled output stage, with an arrow to a box labelled thalamus. An arrow curves from thalamus back to cortex. The loop glows once.
scenes.narration: An output stage feeds the thalamus, which sends an arrow back to the cortex, closing a loop.

scenes.tts: Now the names. The input stage is the striatum. The output stage is the internal globus pallidus, G P I.
scenes.caption: Now the names. The input stage is the striatum. The output stage is the internal globus pallidus, GPi.
scenes.visual: Labels fade in: striatum on the input box, GPi on the output box.
scenes.narration: Now the names. The input stage is the striatum. The output stage is the internal globus pallidus, GPi.

scenes.tts: Its output neurons are inhibitory and fire steadily, even at rest. So the thalamus is held down, like a foot on a brake.
scenes.visual: GPi shows steady firing ticks and a minus chip on the GPi to thalamus arrow. Then GPi is drawn as a foot resting on a brake pedal over the thalamus.
scenes.narration: Its output neurons are inhibitory and fire steadily, even at rest. So the thalamus is held down, like a foot on a brake.

scenes.tts: In the classic model, movement needs the brake lifted.
scenes.visual: The foot lifts a little; the thalamus brightens. Label: movement needs the brake lifted.
scenes.narration: In the classic model, movement needs the brake lifted.

scenes.tts: Two routes run from the striatum to the brake. Striatal projection neurons are inhibitory too.
scenes.visual: Two paths appear between striatum and GPi: a short one straight down and a long one with a detour. A minus chip appears on every arrow leaving the striatum.
scenes.narration: Two routes run from the striatum to the brake. Striatal projection neurons are inhibitory too.

scenes.tts: In the direct route, striatal neurons with D one receptors inhibit the brake. The brake inhibits the thalamus.
scenes.caption: In the direct route, striatal neurons with D1 receptors inhibit the brake. The brake inhibits the thalamus.
scenes.visual: The short path lights up, labelled direct, D1. Two minus chips glow: striatum to GPi, GPi to thalamus.
scenes.narration: In the direct route, striatal neurons with D1 receptors inhibit the brake. The brake inhibits the thalamus.

scenes.tts: Two inhibitions, an even number. More striatal firing releases the thalamus, toward movement.
scenes.visual: The chips flip in turn; the foot lifts; the thalamus brightens. Label: 2 flips, even, toward movement.
scenes.narration: Two inhibitions, an even number. More striatal firing releases the thalamus, toward movement.

scenes.tts: The indirect route takes a detour. Striatal neurons with D two receptors inhibit the external globus pallidus, G P E.
scenes.caption: The indirect route takes a detour. Striatal neurons with D2 receptors inhibit the external globus pallidus, GPe.
scenes.visual: The long path lights up, labelled indirect, D2. A box labelled GPe appears on it.
scenes.narration: The indirect route takes a detour. Striatal neurons with D2 receptors inhibit the external globus pallidus, GPe.

scenes.tts: G P E inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, S T N. And the S T N excites the brake.
scenes.caption: GPe inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, STN. And the STN excites the brake.
scenes.visual: A box labelled STN appears. A minus chip on GPe to STN, a plus chip on STN to GPi.
scenes.narration: GPe inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, STN. And the STN excites the brake.

scenes.tts: Walk it through. D two neurons fire more, so G P E fires less, and the freed S T N fires more.
scenes.caption: Walk it through. D2 neurons fire more, so GPe fires less, and the freed STN fires more.
scenes.visual: Firing ticks change in turn along the detour: D2 faster, GPe slower, STN faster.
scenes.narration: Walk it through. D2 neurons fire more, so GPe fires less, and the freed STN fires more.

scenes.tts: The brake, excited, fires more. The thalamus is held down harder.
scenes.visual: GPi ticks speed up; the foot presses down; the thalamus dims.
scenes.narration: The brake, excited, fires more. The thalamus is held down harder.

scenes.tts: Three inhibitions, an odd number. This route pushes away from movement.
scenes.visual: The three minus chips on the indirect path glow. Label: 3 flips, odd, away from movement.
scenes.narration: Three inhibitions, an odd number. This route pushes away from movement.

scenes.tts: Now add dopamine, from the substantia nigra pars compacta. It acts on the first box of each route. Treat each action as one more link.
scenes.visual: A side box labelled SNc appears and sprays dopamine onto the striatum, at the head of both routes.
scenes.narration: Now add dopamine, from the substantia nigra pars compacta. It acts on the first box of each route. Treat each action as one more link.

scenes.tts: In the classic model, dopamine excites the D one neurons and inhibits the D two neurons.
scenes.caption: In the classic model, dopamine excites the D1 neurons and inhibits the D2 neurons.
scenes.visual: An SNc arrow with a plus chip tints the D1 cells green; an SNc arrow with a minus chip tints the D2 cells red.
scenes.narration: In the classic model, dopamine excites the D1 neurons and inhibits the D2 neurons.

scenes.tts: Acting through each receptor, does dopamine push toward movement or away from it?
scenes.visual: The two dopamine chips pulse. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Acting through each receptor, does dopamine push toward movement or away from it?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; the full chain of chips is visible for each route.

scenes.tts: Toward movement, both ways. Through D one, dopamine adds no flip.
scenes.caption: Toward movement, both ways. Through D1, dopamine adds no flip.
scenes.visual: On screen only: D1 route, 1 excitation then 2 inhibitions, 2 flips, even.
scenes.narration: Toward movement, both ways. Through D1, dopamine adds no flip.

scenes.tts: Through D two, its own inhibition adds one flip to the route's three. Four flips, an even number.
scenes.caption: Through D2, its own inhibition adds one flip to the route's three. Four flips, an even number.
scenes.visual: On screen only: D2 route, dopamine's inhibition, then striatum to GPe, GPe to STN, GPi to thalamus; STN to GPi shown as plus, no flip. 4 flips, even.
scenes.narration: Through D2, its own inhibition adds one flip to the route's three. Four flips, an even number.

scenes.tts: The two actions agree. So losing dopamine pushes both routes toward less movement. The direct route weakens, the indirect strengthens.
scenes.visual: SNc fades out. The direct path dims; the indirect path brightens.
scenes.narration: The two actions agree. So losing dopamine pushes both routes toward less movement. The direct route weakens, the indirect strengthens.

scenes.tts: So the brake fires more for two reasons: less inhibition from the striatum, more excitation from the S T N.
scenes.caption: So the brake fires more for two reasons: less inhibition from the striatum, more excitation from the STN.
scenes.visual: Two arrows press on GPi's foot from two directions: a weaker direct arrow and a stronger STN arrow. The foot presses down.
scenes.narration: So the brake fires more for two reasons: less inhibition from the striatum, more excitation from the STN.

scenes.tts: The thalamus is held down harder, and movement is hard to start: the model's prediction of akinesia.
scenes.visual: The thalamus dims. Label: akinesia, the classic model's prediction.
scenes.narration: The thalamus is held down harder, and movement is hard to start: the model's prediction of akinesia.

scenes.tts: The model rests on a measurement. In nineteen sixty, post-mortem brains from people with Parkinson's disease showed striatal dopamine greatly reduced.
scenes.caption: The model rests on a measurement. In 1960, post-mortem brains from people with Parkinson's disease showed striatal dopamine greatly reduced.
scenes.visual: A schematic bar for striatal dopamine, tall for control brains and much shorter for Parkinson's brains, labelled schematic. Caption on screen: Ehringer and Hornykiewicz, 1960.
scenes.narration: The model rests on a measurement. In 1960, post-mortem brains from people with Parkinson's disease showed striatal dopamine greatly reduced.

scenes.tts: Inhibit an inhibitor, and you release its target.
scenes.visual: End card line: Inhibit an inhibitor and you release its target.
scenes.narration: Inhibit an inhibitor, and you release its target.
